bug_caught_and_fixed.description: generate_run_report.py's NEW_JOBS cutoff used raw STRING comparison between an ISO since cutoff ('...T00:00:00') and jobs.created_at, which SQLite's own DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP writes as a SPACE-separated format ('2026-09-20 16:04:48'). Space (0x20) sorts before 'T' (0x54), so a same-day SQLite-formatted timestamp always string-compared as earlier than an ISO cutoff on the same date, regardless of actual time-of-day.
bug_caught_and_fixed.caught_by: this live run -- new_jobs_count came back 0 when it should have been 1, since the one new job was created the same day as the since cutoff
bug_caught_and_fixed.why_fifth_step_test_missed_it: the FIFTH step's since cutoffs crossed a day boundary, which masked the bug (differing day digits resolve the string comparison before reaching the space-vs-T character)
bug_caught_and_fixed.fix: added generate_run_report._parse_timestamp(), parses both formats into timezone-aware datetime objects (UTC assumed for the naive SQLite form) and compares those, never raw strings
bug_caught_and_fixed.fix_verified: offline, by re-running generate_run_report.generate() against the SAME already-fetched temp DB (zero new network calls) -- new_jobs_count became 1, correctly
